{"node_id":"LVMC_11_52_070","law_refs":["LVMC-11-52-070"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"t1","text":"The City Traffic Engineer shall determine upon what streets angle parking shall be permitted,","role":"condition"},{"id":"t2","text":"and shall provide signage or other markings to indicate where such parking is permitted.","role":"condition"},{"id":"t3","text":"Where angle parking is permitted,","role":"condition"},{"id":"t4","text":"no person shall stand or park a vehicle","role":"obligation"},{"id":"t5","text":"unless the front of the vehicle is pointed toward the direction of lawful traffic movement.","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"t1","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.parking_space","rel.occupies","st.travel_region"],"derived":[],"justification":"The Traffic Engineer's determination of the streets where angle parking is permitted is a legal status no scene shows; the next words name its evidence, the signage or markings. It is read through them: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, \"a point regulation by catalogue code ... angle_parking\") governing (dev.governs, \"the travel regions whose traffic the device controls\") the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), or a marked parking bay (st.parking_space, \"marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute\") whose angle stands clear of zero. The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre (its not-a-stand-in clause)."},{"span":"t2","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.parking_space","rel.occupies","st.travel_region"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"signage\" is the angle_parking regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); \"other markings\" is a marked bay (st.parking_space, \"marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute\") the vehicle occupies whose angle (st_parking_space_angle) stands clear of zero by more than the source's angle resolution. Their presence is the evidence of the permission they indicate."},{"span":"t3","atoms":["dev.regulatory_sign","dev.governs","st.parking_space","rel.occupies","st.travel_region"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"Where angle parking is permitted\" is the place the signage or markings indicate: a travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that an angle_parking sign governs (dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs), or that the vehicle occupies together with an angled marked bay (st.parking_space with its angle clear of zero). Presence of the feature, no size bound: the angle is read only against the source's resolution."},{"span":"t4","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":["drv.motion.parked"],"justification":"Same words and meaning as the mapping index's \"No person shall stand or park a vehicle\" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): drv.motion.parked (\"Road user a is parked: \\\"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\\\"\") with the standing duration as its window, covering standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, \"the halting of a vehicle ... otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers\") and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155); \"a vehicle\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. \"No person\" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion."},{"span":"t5","atoms":["kin.heading","st.lane_direction","rel.occupies","st.travel_region","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic"],"derived":[],"justification":"Same words as the mapping index's \"headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement\" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): \"the front of the vehicle\" points along kin.heading (\"direction the body points\"; not its velocity, so a standing vehicle has one); \"the direction of lawful traffic movement\" is the direction designated for traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, claimed whole as the word's admitted aggregate) on the travel region the vehicle occupies: st.lane_direction (\"direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in\"), read on that region (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). \"pointed toward\" is a positive dot product of the heading with that direction."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) where angle parking is permitted: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign) governs r (dev.governs), or the subject also occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle (st_parking_space_angle), in absolute value, exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.","obligation":"Where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.standing_min_duration)), for every travel region r it occupies that is selected as in the applicability (governed by an angle_parking sign, or occupied together with an angled parking space), the dot product of the subject's heading (kin_heading) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction) is positive: the front of the vehicle points toward the direction of lawful traffic movement. A subject that is not parked complies. Where r carries no direction or the heading is unobserved, the verdict is unknown.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.standing_min_duration","p.parking_space_angle_resolution"],"narrowings":[{"span":"t1","why":"The Traffic Engineer's determination is a legal status read through the signage or markings that display it: a determination no sign or marking displays is not read.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"t2","why":"The duty to provide signage or markings is the Engineer's and is not judged on a trace; the presence of the angle_parking sign or the angled marked bay is read as the indication of where angle parking is permitted.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"t5","why":"\"the direction of lawful traffic movement\" is read as the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies at the angle-parking place; a vehicle wholly inside a bay that overlaps no travel region is not judged.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car has backed into an angled bay (angle 45 degrees) on a street whose lane carries an angle_parking sign; lines: {"node_id":"LVMC_11_52_060","law_refs":["LVMC-11-52-060"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"In no case shall any part of any vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"part of the load of such vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"or trailer","role":"subject"},{"id":"s4","text":"attached to such vehicle","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"project into the street more than fifteen feet measured on a line at right angles to the curb.","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"any vehicle\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (\"every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway\"), claimed whole and never expanded into classes. \"any part of\" the vehicle is any point of its body, whose size kin.extent carries (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"), so the farthest point of the body is what the bound reads. \"In no case\" admits no exception."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"trailer\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer (\"a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle, that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle\"), claimed whole: the trailer is judged as a road user of its own, its body read by the same bound."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"part of the load of such vehicle\" is read through the outline the source reports for the vehicle's body, kin.extent (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"): a load carried on the vehicle within that outline is judged with it; a load overhanging the reported outline is not seen, as the narrowing on span s5 discloses."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway","st.road_edge","st.region_geometry","st.on_way","kin.heading","kin.extent","st.lane_direction","st.travel_region"],"derived":["drv.motion.parked"],"justification":"\"project\" states where a standing body stands out into the street, in a section of the chapter on stopping, standing and parking: it is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, drv.motion.parked (\"Road user a is parked: \\\"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\\\", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation\"); the narrowing discloses the reading. \"street\" is DEF-NRS-484A-265 (\"the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city\", not an aggregate): st.highway (\"the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders\"); its \"not a stand-in for: the roadway\" clause is respected since the definition names the entire width; rel.occupies (\"a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region\") anchors the vehicle on its own street, as the mapping index reads \"upon a street\"; the city limits are the ordinance's own territorial scope. \"more than fifteen feet\" is the stated figure (literal): the body's projection, the ground distance from the curb to its outline (st.region_geometry, \"the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it\") plus the body's own extent across the curb line (kin.extent, \"a formula reads the full length, width and height\"), is compared with it. \"the curb\" is st.road_edge (\"curb or edge of the roadway\") lying on the vehicle's street (st.on_way, \"the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on\"); the curb the vehicle stands at is the road edge of that street nearest its body (st.region_geometry ground distance). \"on a line at right angles to the curb\": the curb runs along the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies (st.lane_direction, \"direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway\"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region), so the body's extent at right angles to the curb is its length (kin.extent) times the absolute cross product of its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) with that direction plus its width times their absolute dot product. The sign of the direction does not matter. st.lane_direction is not used as a manoeuvre or a path: only its line is read; the narrowing on this span discloses the reading."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[{"span":"s4","why":"A trailer is itself \"a vehicle\" by its definition DEF-LVMC-11-02-170, so the duty binds its body through \"any vehicle\" whether or not it is attached; attachment adds no restriction.","scope":"none"}],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"]}],"applicability":"The subject, a vehicle or a trailer (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer), is parked at the observation (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.parking_min_duration)) and its footprint overlaps a highway h (rel.occupies subject h, st.highway): it stands in a street.","obligation":"For every highway h the subject occupies (rel.occupies), every road edge c (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way c h) whose ground distance from the subject's body (st_region_geometry_distance) is at most that of every other road edge lying on h (the curb the vehicle stands at), and every travel region r (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the ground distance from the subject's body to c, plus the subject's length (kin_extent length) times the absolute value of the cross product of its heading (kin_heading x, y) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction x, y), plus its width (kin_extent width) times the absolute value of their dot product, is at most fifteen feet (literal 15 ft). Where r carries no direction, the heading or the geometry is unobserved, the sum is unknown.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.parking_min_duration"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s5","why":"\"project\" is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, parked (at rest for p.parking_min_duration): a vehicle travelling or halted briefly in traffic is not judged, though the words name no state of motion; the section sits among the stopping, standing and parking rules and measures from the curb a vehicle stands at. lines: {"node_id":"LVMC_11_52_060","law_refs":["LVMC-11-52-060"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"In no case shall any part of any vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"part of the load of such vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"or trailer","role":"subject"},{"id":"s4","text":"attached to such vehicle","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"project into the street more than fifteen feet measured on a line at right angles to the curb.","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"any vehicle\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (\"every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway\"), claimed whole and never expanded into classes. \"any part of\" the vehicle is any point of its body, whose size kin.extent carries (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"), so the farthest point of the body is what the bound reads. \"In no case\" admits no exception."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"trailer\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer (\"a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle, that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle\"), claimed whole: the trailer is judged as a road user of its own, its body read by the same bound."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"part of the load of such vehicle\" is read through the outline the source reports for the vehicle's body, kin.extent (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"): a load carried on the vehicle within that outline is judged with it; a load overhanging the reported outline is not seen, as the narrowing on span s5 discloses."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway","st.road_edge","st.region_geometry","st.on_way","kin.heading","kin.extent","st.lane_direction","st.travel_region"],"derived":["drv.motion.parked"],"justification":"\"project\" states where a standing body stands out into the street, in a section of the chapter on stopping, standing and parking: it is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, drv.motion.parked (\"Road user a is parked: \\\"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\\\", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation\"); the narrowing discloses the reading. \"street\" is DEF-NRS-484A-265 (\"the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city\", not an aggregate): st.highway (\"the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders\"); its \"not a stand-in for: the roadway\" clause is respected since the definition names the entire width; rel.occupies (\"a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region\") anchors the vehicle on its own street, as the mapping index reads \"upon a street\"; the city limits are the ordinance's own territorial scope. \"more than fifteen feet\" is the stated figure (literal): the body's projection, the ground distance from the curb to its outline (st.region_geometry, \"the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it\") plus the body's own extent across the curb line (kin.extent, \"a formula reads the full length, width and height\"), is compared with it. \"the curb\" is st.road_edge (\"curb or edge of the roadway\") lying on the vehicle's street (st.on_way, \"the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on\"); lines: {"node_id":"LVMC_11_52_060","law_refs":["LVMC-11-52-060"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"In no case shall any part of any vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"part of the load of such vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"or trailer","role":"subject"},{"id":"s4","text":"attached to such vehicle","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"project into the street more than fifteen feet measured on a line at right angles to the curb.","role":"obligation"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"any vehicle\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (\"every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway\"), claimed whole and never expanded into classes. \"any part of\" the vehicle is any point of its body, whose size kin.extent carries (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"), so the farthest point of the body is what the bound reads. \"In no case\" admits no exception."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"trailer\" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer (\"a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle, that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle\"), claimed whole: the trailer is judged as a road user of its own, its body read by the same bound."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"\"part of the load of such vehicle\" is read through the outline the source reports for the vehicle's body, kin.extent (\"the body's size along its axes about the reference point\"): a load carried on the vehicle within that outline is judged with it; a load overhanging the reported outline is not seen, as the narrowing on span s5 discloses."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.highway","st.road_edge","st.region_geometry","st.on_way","kin.heading","kin.extent","st.lane_direction","st.travel_region"],"derived":["drv.motion.parked"],"justification":"\"project\" states where a standing body stands out into the street, in a section of the chapter on stopping, standing and parking: it is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, drv.motion.parked (\"Road user a is parked: \\\"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\\\", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation\"); the narrowing discloses the reading. \"street\" is DEF-NRS-484A-265 (\"the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city\", not an aggregate): st.highway (\"the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders\"); its \"not a stand-in for: the roadway\" clause is respected since the definition names the entire width; rel.occupies (\"a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region\") anchors the vehicle on its own street, as the mapping index reads \"upon a street\"; the city limits are the ordinance's own territorial scope. \"more than fifteen feet\" is the stated figure (literal): the body's projection, the ground distance from the curb to its outline (st.region_geometry, \"the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it\") plus the body's own extent across the curb line (kin.extent, \"a formula reads the full length, width and height\"), is compared with it. \"the curb\" is st.road_edge (\"curb or edge of the roadway\") lying on the vehicle's street (st.on_way, \"the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on\"); the curb the vehicle stands at is the road edge of that street nearest its body (st.region_geometry ground distance). \"on a line at right angles to the curb\": the curb runs along the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies (st.lane_direction, \"direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway\"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region), so the body's extent at right angles to the curb is its length (kin.extent) times the absolute cross product of its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) with that direction plus its width times their absolute dot product. The sign of the direction does not matter. st.lane_direction is not used as a manoeuvre or a path: only its line is read; the narrowing on this span discloses the reading."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[{"span":"s4","why":"A trailer is itself \"a vehicle\" by its definition DEF-LVMC-11-02-170, so the duty binds its body through \"any vehicle\" whether or not it is attached; attachment adds no restriction.","scope":"none"}],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer"]}],"applicability":"The subject, a vehicle or a trailer (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer), is parked at the observation (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.parking_min_duration)) and its footprint overlaps a highway h (rel.occupies subject h, st.highway): it stands in a street.","obligation":"For every highway h the subject occupies (rel.occupies), every road edge c (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way c h) whose ground distance from the subject's body (st_region_geometry_distance) is at most that of every other road edge lying on h (the curb the vehicle stands at), and every travel region r (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the ground distance from the subject's body to c, plus the subject's length (kin_extent length) times the absolute value of the cross product of its heading (kin_heading x, y) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction x, y), plus its width (kin_extent width) times the absolute value of their dot product, is at most fifteen feet (literal 15 ft). Where r carries no direction, the heading or the geometry is unobserved, the sum is unknown.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.parking_min_duration"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s5","why":"\"project\" is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, parked (at rest for p.parking_min_duration): a vehicle travelling or halted briefly in traffic is not judged, though the words name no state of motion; the section sits among the stopping, standing and parking rules and measures from the curb a vehicle stands at. # Plan — batch 06 (LVMC 11.52.060, 11.52.070, 11.52.130 (A)(2), (4), (5), (7), (11), (12))

No law-local aggregates (`aggregates.jsonl` is empty). No new concept records: the nodes reuse
`drv.motion.complete_halt` and `drv.motion.parked`, which an earlier batch of this iteration proposed.

## LVMC_11_52_060 — projection into street (coded)

**Decision.** There is one node with one obligation span: "project into the street more than fifteen feet
measured on a line at right angles to the curb." The subject is a vehicle or a trailer, both
claimed as their admitted aggregates.
- "project" is read for a vehicle that is **parked** (`drv.motion.parked` with
  `p.halt_speed_tolerance`, `p.parking_min_duration`). The section sits in the
  stopping/standing/parking chapter and measures from the curb the vehicle stands at. Read
  literally, every vehicle driving in a lane more than fifteen feet from the curb would violate.
- "street" (DEF-NRS-484A-265) is `st.highway` anchored by `rel.occupies`, as the mapping index
  already reads it.
- "the curb" is the `st.road_edge` lying on that street (`st.on_way`) that is nearest the body.
- The projection is the body-to-curb ground distance (`st.region_geometry`) plus the body's extent
  across the curb line. That extent is length·|heading × dir| + width·|heading · dir|, where dir is
  the designated direction (`st.lane_direction`) of the travel region the vehicle occupies. That
  direction is read as the curb's line, and the reading is disclosed.
- A load is judged only inside the body outline the source reports. That limit is disclosed as a
  narrowing, because no atom carries an overhanging load.
- "attached to such vehicle" is a scope-none residue: a trailer is "a vehicle" by DEF-LVMC-11-02-170,
  so its own body is judged whether or not it is attached.

**What would reverse it.** If a labelled moving vehicle is judged under 11.52.060, drop the parked
reading. If an ontology atom for a curb's direction or for a load overhang is added, use it in
place of the carrier direction or kin.extent.

## LVMC_11_52_070 — angle parking (coded)

**Decision.** There is one node.
- The Traffic Engineer's determination and the duty to sign or mark the streets are not road-user
  duties. They are read as `status` observable readings: what shows them is an `angle_parking`
  regulatory sign governing the occupied travel region, or an occupied marked bay whose angle
  stands clear of zero. "Clear of zero" uses the new parameter `p.parking_space_angle_resolution`,
  which only states the source's resolution. The same mapping as the index precedent "The City
  Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine…" applies.
- The obligation span reuses the index mapping of "No person shall stand or park a vehicle"
  (`drv.motion.parked` with `p.standing_min_duration`). It also reuses the index mapping of
  "headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement" (`kin.heading`, `st.lane_direction`,
  `rel.occupies`, `st.travel_region`, traffic aggregate).
- "Front pointed toward" is a positive dot product of heading and designated direction on every
  selected travel region the vehicle occupies.
- A vehicle wholly inside a bay that overlaps no travel region is not judged. This is disclosed as
  a reading.

**What would reverse it.** If the source's `st_parking_space_angle` is not measured from the curb
line (for example, 90° for a parallel bay), the bay-angle test must change. A label that judges a
vehicle that is entirely within a bay would require a different direction source.

## LVMC_11_52_130 (A)(2), (A)(4), (A)(5), (A)(7), (A)(11), (A)(12) — no stopping at places (gapped)

**Decision.** All six share one preamble, and it is segmented the same way in each node:
- **"stop, stand or park".** "Stop" is prohibited here, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies by its own
  scope ("when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily"). The three verbs together therefore
  mean any halt: `drv.motion.complete_halt`. The index maps "No person shall stand or park" to
  `drv.motion.parked`; the word "stop" is why this mapping differs.
- **"except when necessary to avoid conflict … with other traffic".** This is a standard. It is
  operationalized by a road user of traffic (the admitted aggregate) ahead in the same lane within
  `p.queue_halt_gap` (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`, `rel.surface_gap`). Reading conflict only as
  traffic ahead in the lane is disclosed as a narrowing.
- **"the directions of a police officer".** `dev.human_direction` with role police_officer and
  indication stop, governing the occupied region. This is the index mapping.
- **"a traffic control device".** A stop sign, yield sign, red/yellow signal or active railway
  signal or gate governing the occupied region.
- **"in compliance with law" is an `operator` gap.** It excepts any halt that another law requires:
  yielding to a pedestrian at a crosswalk, stopping before the sidewalk when emerging from a
  driveway, stopping for a school bus or an emergency vehicle. No atom carries this, and
  `Formula.rule` composes only one named rule. The composable candidates are all "not composable"
  this iteration. The open gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22 proposes the same operator for the same
  words. Dropping the exception would make A12 and A11 report every lawful yield at a crosswalk or
  intersection as a violation. So all six nodes carry the gap and are not coded.

Places and their own gaps:
- **A11.** `st.intersection` and `st.region_geometry` within the literal fifteen feet.
- **A12.** Marked `st.crosswalk` within the literal twenty feet.
- **A2.** `st.curb_zone` of kind fire_lane, occupied. The designation and posting are a status
  reading. The Fire Code reference is out of the corpus and is a residue. "attended or unattended"
  and "public or private property" are scope-none residues.
- **A4.** `st.fire_hydrant` within a bound chosen by `Term.cond`: twenty feet where an
  angle-parking or no-parking sign, an angled bay or a no-parking/no-stopping/fire-lane zone
  applies, otherwise fifteen feet. The "posted / painted red / public or private" clauses are
  scope-none residues.
- **A5.** Has a second gap, an atom gap `st.sidewalk_elevator_or_chute`. `st.obstruction` kind
  sidewalk_fixture cannot tell an elevator from a bench. The frontage is read with the new
  parameter `p.curb_frontage_reach` and with `prim.region_offset_along` within five feet plus half
  the vehicle's length.
- **A7.** Has three further atom gaps:
  - `st.driveway_entrance`: the contract of `st.driveway_or_alley_entrance` says it cannot tell a
    driveway from an alley.
  - `rel.premises_privilege`: the exemption for the driveway's owner, controller, family or
    invitee.
  - `ru.postal_vehicle`: `ru.official_vehicle` has no postal kind.

  Also on A7:
